hackathons.description:
### Overview
**OpenCV AI Competition 2026, powered by AWS** is an innovation challenge hosted by **The Open Source Vision Foundation (OpenCV), sponsored by AWS**, conducted entirely online with global participation. Designed for ambitious developers, designers, and problem solvers, this hackathon invites creators to form cross-functional teams and build working software prototypes that address critical real-world friction points.

### Focus Tracks & Challenge Areas
Participants are encouraged to build high-impact applications within any of the following official domains:
• **AI & Intelligent Systems**: Build autonomous agents, computer vision pipelines, or LLM-powered applications that solve tangible domain challenges.
• **Open Innovation & Impact**: Freedom to build any software or hardware prototype that creates high-impact outcomes for communities and businesses.
• **Social Good & Public Infrastructure**: Solutions improving civic engagement, accessibility, educational equity, and government public services.

### Competition Format & Stages
The event is structured into three continuous phases:
1. **Registration & Project Ideation**: Complete registration, formulate team rosters (1–5 members), and submit problem statement choices.
2. **Prototype Sprint**: Rapid engineering sprint with scheduled mentor office hours to review architecture, codebase quality, and user experience.
3. **Showcase & Evaluation**: Final pitch demonstrations where finalists showcase live demos before an esteemed panel of industry judges.

### Eligibility & Team Rules
• **Team Composition**: Open to individual builders or teams of 1–5 members. Multidisciplinary skillsets (fullstack, UI/UX, data science) are highly recommended.
• **Eligibility**: Age 13+, parental permission if under age of majority; excluded: Brazil residents, organizer staff
• **Original Work**: All code and designs submitted must be authored during the hackathon period. Open-source libraries and public frameworks are permitted with clear attribution.

### Submission Checklist
All final submissions must provide:
1. Public Git repository containing clean source code and documentation.
2. 3-minute recorded video walkthrough explaining the problem, solution, and architecture.
3. Presentation slide deck (PDF or link) outlining market viability and future roadmap.
4. Live deployed URL, hosted web application, or installable APK.

### Overview
**Google Cloud Tech Camp** is an innovation challenge hosted by **Hack2skill Event Host**, hosted on-site. Designed for ambitious developers, designers, and problem solvers, this hackathon invites creators to form cross-functional teams and build working software prototypes that address critical real-world friction points.

### Focus Tracks & Challenge Areas
Participants are encouraged to build high-impact applications within any of the following official domains:
• **Developer Tools & Cloud Architecture**: Streamline engineering workflows, build developer-first platforms, or create resilient cloud infrastructure.
• **Open Innovation & Impact**: Freedom to build any software or hardware prototype that creates high-impact outcomes for communities and businesses.
• **Social Good & Public Infrastructure**: Solutions improving civic engagement, accessibility, educational equity, and government public services.

### Competition Format & Stages
The event is structured into three continuous phases:
1. **Registration & Project Ideation**: Complete registration, formulate team rosters (1–4 members), and submit problem statement choices.
2. **Prototype Sprint**: Rapid engineering sprint with scheduled mentor office hours to review architecture, codebase quality, and user experience.
3. **Showcase & Evaluation**: Final pitch demonstrations where finalists showcase live demos before an esteemed panel of industry judges.

### Eligibility & Team Rules
• **Team Composition**: Open to individual builders or teams of 1–4 members. Multidisciplinary skillsets (fullstack, UI/UX, data science) are highly recommended.
• **Eligibility**: Check official page on Hack2skill
• **Original Work**: All code and designs submitted must be authored during the hackathon period. Open-source libraries and public frameworks are permitted with clear attribution.

### Submission Checklist
All final submissions must provide:
1. Public Git repository containing clean source code and documentation.
2. 3-minute recorded video walkthrough explaining the problem, solution, and architecture.
3. Presentation slide deck (PDF or link) outlining market viability and future roadmap.
4. Live deployed URL, hosted web application, or installable APK.
